"I can book my own flight why do I need an Agent"

You DON'T need an Agent of course, silly to think that you would need AI Agents to do things you can do today.

What I've seen that Agents help a lot in general is reducing context switching:

My @openclaw work Agent triages all incoming requests for me. Coworkers saying "Where are Damian's OKRs?" "Can Damian do a PR review?" "This prototype X finished?" etc etc that my Agent triages for me "Here's the link for his OKRs" "I've done a first PR Pass to the PR as Damian would", "Prototype is mid sprint according to the clickup backlog" followed by "and I can add your request to his backlog if you need his help". 

My Agent then puts the request in my triage queue "Review PR is P1, Finalizing OKR is P0.." It saves ME so much context switch, which has been the #1 issue as an engineer at ANY company I've worked in. Stopping what I'm doing to answer that "Hi Damian sorry to bother you with..." random pings I used to get on Slack.

Now? They all hit my personal agent, who triages it for me. If it's really urgent either my Agent or the person themselves ask me directly, everything else gets automatically triaged. I pull from the backlog, get shit done and am less annoyed by the interruptions that I used to get.

So, saying "I can book my own flight why do I need an Agent" is a tiny bit of what Agents can do for you. 

Think Bigger. Think Together.

今天也尝试使用 Grok Bot 自动 X 搜集信息制作视频，为了让视频更稳定，我让 Grok Bot 安装了 Baitu-Video Skill，具体教程如下：

直接把下面这段话发给 Grok Bot：
「每天早上 9 点（台北时间），用你自带的 X 搜索，帮我扫一遍过去 18 小时 X 上最热的 AI 消息，包括新产品发布和好用的功能推荐。优先看 OpenAI、Anthropic、Google DeepMind、Cursor 这类官方号和靠谱博主，别搜币圈那些垃圾帖。按点赞、转发、收藏、引用算热度，同一件事只留最热的一条，挑出 6 条主线，再加几条值得扫一眼的放进雷达。每个数字都去官方核实，没查到的标未证实，不许编。」

3️⃣ 让 Grok Bot 把扫到的内容做成视频

text:
免费白嫖 Meta Muse Agent 却苦于沙箱频繁重启、数据无法落地？

我用 OCI 免费 ARM + shell2http 给它接了条“外挂手臂”，中间却连续踩了 2 个极其隐蔽的 Agent 架构天坑。

把完整的穿透方案与避坑复盘写在这里：

1. 痛点：被关在笼子里的沙箱 Agent

Meta Muse 免费版很好用，但沙箱生命周期极短，虚拟机重启就丢上下文和落盘数据。

我手头正好有一台闲置的 Oracle Cloud (OCI) 2C12G ARM 实例，非常适合给 Muse 做持久化算力和存储宿主。

但刚上手就撞上网络高墙： Muse 的网络出口经过代理发布，封死了 SSH 22 端口，甚至直连自定义 IP 端口也全面受限。

2. 破局：极轻量穿透组合

既然不能直连，就走 HTTP 内网穿透反向代理。

我在 OCI 上跑了 shell2http：

Go 原生静态编译，ARM64 运行内存仅占 1.2 MB，几乎零资源消耗。
只监听本地端口，通过 Cloudflare Tunnel 打通公网 HTTPS 路由。
外部机器彻底免开防火墙端口，安全且极其优雅。

3. 天坑一：CF Service Token 与 Agent Vault 冲突

为了安全，第一反应是用 Cloudflare 的 Service Token 做边缘拦截。

结果配置时撞墙： Muse Vault 的凭证存储逻辑是单 URL 只能存 1 条记录。 而 CF 的 Service Token 必须同时塞 CF-Access-Client-Id 和 CF-Access-Client-Secret 两个 Header。

解法：果断调整架构，关闭 Tunnel 的 Access 验证，退回由 shell2http 原生接管 HTTP Basic Auth。 标准化的单行认证串，100% 兼容各类 Agent 凭证库。

4. 天坑二：Vault 凭证不等于 Shell 环境变量

凭证存进 Vault 后，命令依然调不通，这是最隐蔽的坑：

许多人以为 Vault 会自动打进系统的全局环境变量。 但实际上 Muse Vault 的设计是给“系统级 Tool”自动注入的，根本不会注入给 muse.exec 的裸 curl！

解法：不要在命令行死磕。 直接让 Muse 自己在内部生成一个专属 Skill，把调用封装为原生工具。 这样 Vault 凭证会在 Skill 执行时自动注入，一键彻底打通！

💡 TL;DR 核心经验

• 轻量即正义：给沙箱 Agent 外挂环境，shell2http (1.2MB) + CF Tunnel 远比厚重的 SSH Jump 或 API 服务省心。 • 鉴权向 Agent 妥协：面对严格限制单字段的凭证管理器，标准的 Basic Auth 比多 Header 的 Token 更具通用性。 • 遵守平台范式：Vault 不进裸 Bash，把远程交互包装成 Agent 自带的 Skill 才是正统路径。

你在给沙箱 Agent（如 Muse、Claude Code、Devin 等）桥接外部资源时，还遇到过哪些网络或鉴权怪坑？

关注 @YajunZhu36691 获取更多 AI Agent 实战复盘与架构见解。

Took me 3 months to connect Buzz to my Hermes agent. I almost quit twice. Zero regrets.

Background: I have a Hermes agent that manages my projects, research, and a bunch of automations. It lives on my PC. The problem was access, I could only really talk to it from that machine.

Buzz seemed like the obvious fix: agent joins a channel, I message him, done. In practice, connecting it was three months of pain. Auth, keys, relay behavior, one stretch where messages showed up in an activity feed but never in the chat itself, which took weeks to figure out. There were two moments where I genuinely considered dropping the whole idea.

What kept me going was the picture in my head: managing my agent from my phone, from anywhere, like sending a text.

That's literally what I have now. I'm writing this from my phone while my agent works on something I asked for an hour ago. When he's done, it'll be waiting in the thread.

If you're sitting on a half-finished integration like this, my advice: finish it. The last 10% is where I almost gave up and it's also the part that made the whole thing worth it.

how I decide if a new AI tool is worth adding, now that my feed throws a few at me every day (non-dev, one agent for office work)

I paste the link to my agent, Hermes Agent with Claude underneath, and ask "useful for me or not", it reads the site and answers against what I actually run, and it checks the same three things every time

- how many agents would use it, because the gateways that share your logins across agents mean nothing when you run one
- does it reach the app I live in all day, at work my email only works through the desktop app, so anything that wants cloud access to my mail is out
- does my agent already do it, like a vault for logins, approval before sensitive actions, its own connections to the tools I use

last one I asked about was Executor, a YC gateway that connects any agent to anything, and the answer was not now, maybe later if I end up running a second agent around the clock on another PC

what I got wrong before was patching the agent's own code to make things work, when I had it list my local fixes a few of them would have been wiped by the next update, so now I only touch settings and skills, never the core

if you want a first step, ask your agent to list every change you made to it and which ones survive an update, what's the last tool you added and then removed?

text:
I have been using @OpenAI dots for a little while, here are some thoughts and tips: 

- I have connected my email via the gmail connector and it's great. It pings me whenever an important info is there. Great to dig through past mails and find buried information. 

- So far it seems pretty well aligned. It sticks to the rights I am giving it and ask for my approval whenever there is a sensitive action to take. 

- As an Apple user I have been quite frustrated with integrating stuff like Apple Calendar, Notes,  Reminders... There is no plugins in codex for those. I first tried some work around using some CLIs I found on GitHub but it ended being a mess. My computer always had to be awake for something to work and some permission access would drop from time to time.

- For Calendar I found a good solution which is to connect the google calendar plugin, have my dot use that plugin and sync my Apple Calendar with my Google Calendar. Works great.

- For Reminders I couldn't find anything decent to keep Apple Reminders. So I resigned and had my dot transfer all my reminders to To Do Ist instead and have it use the plugin. Didn't test extensively yet but it seems to work ok.

- For Notes I didn't find any satisfactory solution yet and I am trying to avoid as much as possible to go back to Notion (way too bloated as I remember it). I don't use Notes that much so it's pending for now. 

- Otherwise it's pretty useful at being an orchestrator for coding agents. It kicks off subagents, keep then going once they are done and holds all of the context across my projects. It's essentially working 24/7. Not perfect, some issues from time to time but it's interesting.

- I have configured my Action Button on my phone to open my dot in dictation mode (using Apple Shortcuts). That one is VERY handy. U press, u speak and done.

 Hey, kick off this eval.
 Hey, create this event.
 Hey, remind me to do this. 
 Hey, what was this paper I read that did X?

- Pretty useful too for cron jobs: daily news, job opportunities relevant for me and what not. 

- Cool for proactive stuff also. You can have it do stuff from time to time like analyzing your repos every day to look for issues, look at the latest HF datasets that dropped on topic X yadayada.

- Great for long term memory, it remembers a ton of things. It finally feels like you are not loosing your context anymore.

- It's very capable at computer use (on its own computer). I had it fill some forms for me to remove my phone number from databases. But you can use that for really anything doable on a computer. It can even create your diagrams on Inkscape over there.

- It's not perfect tho, sometimes connection with my local computer is dropping  and it can struggle with its codex threads too (selecting the right model and all).

TODAY I LET GROK BOT MAKE EVERY SINGLE PHONE CALL FOR ME, AND I CAN’T F*CKING BELIEVE WHAT HAPPENED

I decided to run an experiment.

Yesterday Elon posted that Grok Bot can now call people and businesses for you, make a request on your behalf and send you a summary of the conversation.

So I tested it on my real life. Here’s how my day went:

→ INTERNET PROVIDER: I told my bot my bill was too high.

It called, sat through the menu, asked to be transferred to retention and calmly said I was thinking about switching. 28 minutes later: $35 off every month.

Then it did something I would never think of: it asked about hidden fees and made them confirm the new price by email. I just read the live transcript like a Netflix show.

→ GYM MEMBERSHIP: the one you can “only cancel by phone”.

They tried to keep me three times. A discount, a free month, a “pause instead”. My bot said no to all of it, got the cancellation confirmed and sent me the confirmation number.

I’d been too lazy to deal with it for two weeks straight. Grok Bot just handled it for me.

→ BARBER: I needed a fresh cut before the evening.

My bot called my barber and booked me for 5 PM. He chatted with it like with a regular client, said “see you later, bro” and hung up.

He still doesn’t know he was talking to a bot.

→ AND THEN IT GOT CRAZY: I asked it to plan a date.

First it called a restaurant and booked a table for two at 8 PM. Then it called my girlfriend and invited her to dinner, at the exact place it had just booked.

She said yes. Then she texted me “did your AI just ask me out?”

Total: almost 2 hours on the phone today. I spent 0 of them.

This update is absolutely insane, and I’m still in shock from this experiment. Calls were the last thing I still had to do myself. Now Grok Bot does them better than I do.

Bookmark this so you can try the same experiment yourself.

And I broke down all the latest major Grok Bot updates in my article below ↓

text:
I’d built a slew of agents on codex to help me reduce some cognitive load and they were working really well. With the introduction of dots (who are always on) I decided to try moving over. It’s been a surprisingly underwhelming experience for a few reasons:

1. My dot is not proactive. I constantly have to ask my dot about things I asked it to do rather than it surface those things to me. It feels like I have yet another person to manage versus someone who is managing my life. 

2. My dot doesn’t seem to know me. I’ve fed it a lot of context before we started and for some reason it doesn’t really use that when engaging. Feels like I’m just talking to some random person versus someone who knows me and how I operate. 

3. My dot doesn’t seem very smart. It told me I was missing an integration so I went and added it and told it so. It left the original request blocked until I asked why we hadn’t gotten that thing done. More intern behavior than chief of staff behavior. 

4. My dot waits for me to engage. I’ll often have to follow up on what’s next or waiting for me versus have it manage where to focus. Muse actually does this really well without being annoying. Dot’s could learn a lot here.

5. I wish my dot helped me get better at using dots. OAI has so many product names, I often get lost (dots, spaces, work, codex, gpt, etc). Why doesn’t my dot help me figure out how to use the universe of OAI products better, including other dots!

Hoping this gets much better in some of these ways! Cc @thsottiaux
use_case_summary_en: Moved a set of working Codex agents (for reducing cognitive load) to always-on Dots and found the experience surprisingly underwhelming.
use_case_summary_zh: 把原本在 Codex 上运行良好的一组减负智能体迁移到常驻的 Dots，体验却出乎意料地平庸。

text:
I got access to Claude Duet and I've been playing with it.

It's pretty impressive, especially considering how smart Opus 5.5 is. But I'm a bit disappointed that it's a separate app and doesn't connect to the Claude desktop app or have access to my local files.

With OpenAI Dots, I can ask it to create or edit files on my computer, and when I open my laptop, everything is already there. I actually use this a lot.

I also managed to get my Dot to make phone calls for me. I asked it to integrate Twilio with OpenAI's Live API and a clone of my voice. It called my barber, who doesn't even have a website, and booked me a haircut. No third-party booking service, just an actual phone call.

My next experiment is giving it the ability to answer my incoming calls and access my voicemails.

For things like handling email, I think Duet and Dots are pretty comparable. But without desktop integration, I don't see myself using Duet nearly as much as Dots.

Which is a shame because I genuinely think it could be huge with Opus 5.5 behind it.
use_case_summary_en: Got access to Claude Duet and finds it impressive, but is disappointed it is a separate app without access to the Claude desktop app or local files.
